questions.question: What does it mean for $E$ to be sequentially compact in a metric space?
options: Every sequence in $E$ is constant, never varying.
Every sequence has a subsequence converging in $E$.
questions.explanation: A set $E$ is sequentially compact when every sequence in $E$ has a subsequence converging to a point of $E$. In metric spaces, this is equivalent to compactness.
questions.source_support: The definition states that every sequence in $E$ has a convergent subsequence with limit in $E$.

Subsequences in $E$ need not diverge; sequential compactness requires some subsequence to converge.
